title: security-eng-sync-notes-2026-03-07
content:
Security Engineering Weekly Sync - 2026-03-07
Attendees: Avery Chen (owner), Jordan Patel, Riley Thompson, Samir Ali, Maya Rodriguez, guest: infra oncall (H. Lee)
Location: Zoom / #sec-engineering

1) Quick status & context
- Current focus: vuln triage backlog, secrets sprawl initiative, threat modeling for Private deployment v2.
- Notable: transient increase in low-severity findings from dependency scan after dependency bump; no active exploitation indicators.
- Oncall update (H. Lee): brief network flapping during weekend in us-west-2 caused delayed alert delivery, but no security impact. Incident doc will be linked.

2) Vulnerability triage (JIRA: SEC-457, SEC-462)
- SEC-457: dependency "fast-serialize" v2.1.3 shows moderate RCE pattern in scanner. Repro attempted in sandbox by Riley: no exploit path in our runtime due to sandboxed pipeline, but library is used in internal tooling (not customer-facing) - action: Riley to open PR to upgrade to v2.1.6 and run full e2e tests (owner: Riley, due: 2026-03-10).
- SEC-462: reported SNYK high on image base (alpine -> glibc CVE). Samir validated that affected package versions not present in our prod images; however build images used by some engineers do include vulnerable package. Action: Samir + infra to rotate build images and update Dockerfile base to fixed tag (owner: Samir & H. Lee, due: 2026-03-12).
- Triage process reminder: low/medium findings without exploitability in our environment -> annotate with "context-no-exploit" and schedule for weekly cleanup; high/critical -> block PR and create incident if customer impact.

3) Secrets management / secrets sprawl (project kickoff)
- Summary: discovery script run across repos and CI returned ~14 findings (plain text tokens, old AWS keys, slack webhooks). Bulk are expired or test tokens but some need remediation.
- Decision: adopt the following short-term process: (1) rotate any still-active credentials immediately, (2) mark findings in JIRA (SEC-470) and assign repo owners, (3) add pre-commit scanning (git-secrets) into onboarding template and CI.
- Actions:
  - Maya to own rotation list and coordinate with repo owners for the next 2 weeks (owner: Maya, due: 2026-03-14).
  - Jordan to draft updated onboarding checklist with git-secrets + example config (owner: Jordan, due: 2026-03-11).
  - Engineering enablement: create short playbook for developers showing how to remove secrets from git history (BFG / git-filter-repo), include safe rollback steps (owner: Avery, due: 2026-03-18).
- Note: discussed tradeoff for strict blocking in CI vs staged rollout. Agreed to start with warning-level failures for one week, then escalate to fail-on-detect if noise is low.

4) Threat modeling for Private deployment v2 (design review prep)
- Context: Private v2 will introduce customer-managed KMS passthrough and optional on-prem control plane. Need threat model focused on: key leakage, supply-chain for on-prem installer, network egress controls, and admin access footprint.
- Drafts: Riley presented initial attack surface map (shared in Confluence). Key open questions: how do we authenticate bootstrap agents? Can we avoid long-lived provisioning tokens?
- Decisions / next steps:
  - Use short-lived signed CSR approach for agent bootstrap (prototype required). Action: Riley to prototype CSR flow + write up security assumptions for design review (owner: Riley, due: 2026-03-21).
  - Threat modeling workshop scheduled 2026-03-16, 9:30-11:00 PST (invite sent). All eng leads + compliance to attend.

5) Detections & monitoring
- False-positive spike in anomaly detector after new traffic pattern from Dedicated customers. Jordan to tune detector thresholds and add a suppression rule for known pattern (owner: Jordan, due: 2026-03-09).
- Alerting playbook: update runbooks to include next steps for "secrets detected in repo" and "build-image vulnerability". Action: Samir to update runbooks in Confluence (owner: Samir, due: 2026-03-13).

6) Operational items / housekeeping
- Quarterly pentest scheduling: vendor availability confirmed for 2026-04-20 to 2026-04-24. Need to collate asset list by 2026-03-20. Action: Avery to send asset list request to product and infra teams (owner: Avery, due: 2026-03-12).
- SLA / Dedicated customers: compile recent latency/security tickets before next customer review (owner: Maya, due: 2026-03-15).

7) Action item summary (short list)
- Riley: upgrade fast-serialize + prototype CSR flow + threat model writeup (SEC-457, prototype due 2026-03-21).
- Samir & H. Lee: rotate build images + update Dockerfile base (due 2026-03-12).
- Maya: rotate any active secrets, assemble asset list for pentest, compile SLA tickets (due dates above).
- Jordan: onboarding checklist + tune anomaly detector (due 2026-03-11 and 2026-03-09).
- Avery: onboarding playbook for history rewrite + send pentest asset request (due 2026-03-18 / 2026-03-12).

8) Open questions / parking lot
- How aggressive should we be with CI blocking for secret detection without breaking developer velocity? (Action: experiment with warning -> fail rollout and measure false positive rate).
- Do we need dedicated secrets-proxy for Private customers? Parking for architecture discussion after threat-model workshop.

Next sync: 2026-03-14, same time.
Notes saved to Confluence link and JIRA tickets opened for tracked items.

Quick links / refs:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Security+Runbook
- JIRA: SEC-457, SEC-462, SEC-470
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1284 (fast-serialize upgrade draft)
- Slack thread: #sec-engineering (thread pinned)

End of notes.
